title: Triage review of c34's two-kind Marangoni trait swap: on fresh seed 7 every rod is kind B from the first frames in both the swap arm and the neutral twin, so this seed cannot test the selection claim; no kind conversions and B-only divisions (23 and 24 persistent splits)
summary: I re-ran the finding's world with labkit on fresh seed 7 (185 frames, 128^2) in the swap arm (WORLD_P mar 0, marB 40: B swims) and the neutral twin (mar 40, marB 40), and scored both with the finding's kinds.py and switches.py (results_c36.txt). The world runs as described: rods nucleate from noise and divide, and no rod switches kind along any labkit track (0 switches in 86 and 88 pure-kind tracks). But on this seed all rods are kind B from frame 16 to the end in both arms (A share of pure rods 0.00 throughout), so the swimming kind's gain over the neutral twin cannot be measured: B holds 100% in both. Persistent splits by parent kind: B 23 (swap) and 24 (neutral), A 0. The founders' kinds are set by the initial sA/sB noise, and seed 7's noise gives no surviving A founders.

seeds_run.note: all rods kind B from frame 16 in both arms; no A founders, so no share comparison possible; 0 kind switches

not_checked: F (the swimmer-share gain) on a seed with both kinds present
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed that happened to give single-kind founders; it neither supports nor contradicts the 6/6 paired comparisons. It does show that founder kind composition is seed-dependent, so a pre-registered seed set (or a founder balance check) would make the paired test robust.
